   "Agentic commerce is a long-duration transition (3-5+ years) that will gradually reshape the consumer shopping journey from discovery to autonomous purchasing.",
   "Value will increasingly follow consumer intent; the strategic battle shifts to who owns discovery and the infrastructure required to convert intent into a trusted transaction.",
   "Early adoption is concentrated in low-risk, commoditized categories (e.g., CPG, staples), while subjective categories like luxury and apparel will progress more slowly.",

 {
  "source": "Harding Loevner",
  "title": "What We Talk About When We Talk About Momentum",
  "type": "strategy",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-09-27",
  "insights": [
   "Momentum is a meta-signal reflecting market capital flows rather than a stable company attribute like quality, growth, or value.",
   "The content of momentum is unstable, meaning a momentum-based portfolio can shift from high-quality growth stocks to speculative cyclicals or commodity producers without changing its factor label.",
   "Fundamental investors often use momentum as a confirmation bias tool, mistaking price appreciation for validation of their thesis rather than independent evidence of business progress.",
   "Quantitative investors risk treating momentum as a stable premium, potentially accumulating exposure to crowded regime trades without identifying the underlying concentration risk.",
   "Momentum reversals are often violent because strategies own the same recent winners, leading to simultaneous exits when market regimes turn.",
   "Investors must interpret the underlying drivers of momentum exposure rather than treating it as an intrinsic characteristic of the companies involved."
  ],
  "risks": [
   "Crowded regime trades",
   "Confirmation bias in fundamental analysis",
   "Misinterpretation of momentum as a stable factor premium",
   "Violent momentum reversals during regime shifts"
